newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to join project with phone links to China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to join project with phone links to China.

text.p: Taiwan's state-run Chunghwa Telecommunication Corp will join an Asia-Pacific cable network project that would enable a potential direct telephone link with the island's political rival China, officials said on Monday.
"Chunghwa Telecommunication will participate in an Asia-Pacific cable network, and communist China will also join the project," said an official at the Ministry of Transportation and Communications.
The network would be completed by early 2000 and would make it possible for Taiwan and China to establish direct telephone links if both governments agree, the official said.
Direct telephone links between the two sides are banned. Taiwan's telephone connection with China are now routed through Hong Kong or other third countries.
Chunghwa Telecommunication officials declined to comment.
Local media reported that the network would have about 1,890 telephone lines in capacity to connect Taiwan's southern town of Fangshan and China's southeastern city of Guangzhou.
Taiwan has banned direct transport, communications and other official links with communist China for nearly five decades, but faces mounting pressure from Taiwan firms to ease the restriction.
Some 25,000 Taiwan firms have poured US$20 billion into China since an unofficial thaw a decade ago. Indirect trade across the Taiwan Strait has soared.
Hong Kong remains the main transshipment centre for links between Taiwan and China, but Taiwan is actively seeking a alternative as the British colony's handover looms in mid-1997.
